headline: The two sets · 13:26

items.title: 13:26 · To see how the five-tier machine hides
items.detail: To see how the five-tier machine hides inside everyday racial language, we walk the set-theoretic ladder developed in Section 2.1 of Chapter 2.

items.title: 13:35 · We begin with the experimental baseline of
items.detail: We begin with the experimental baseline of group categorization.

items.title: 13:44 · Tajfel assigned participants to arbitrary groups on
items.detail: Tajfel assigned participants to arbitrary groups on trivial criteria, such as preferences for abstract paintings by Klee or Kandinsky or estimates of dots flashed on a screen.

items.title: 13:55 · Participants had zero face-to-face interaction zero shared
items.detail: Participants had zero face-to-face interaction, zero shared history, and zero personal material stake in the group labels.

items.title: 14:02 · Even under those stripped-down conditions subjects consistently
items.detail: Even under those stripped-down conditions, subjects consistently favored their assigned ingroup and maximized the relative gap between ingroup and outgroup rewards.
